video.title: The Fantasy Basketball BUSTS You Need To Avoid | The Suckiest Bunch of Sucks That Ever Sucked

summary: Josh Lloyd lists players he thinks are overvalued ("busts") in Yahoo rankings and ADP as of October 6, first for points leagues and then for 9-category leagues. He stresses that Yahoo's single ranking is not tied to any format, so you need to adjust for your own scoring. His points league busts include Tyrese Maxey, Kevin Durant, Tyrese Haliburton, Trae Young, Donovan Mitchell, Steph Curry, Chet Holmgren, Payton Pritchard and AJ Dybantsa. His category busts include Cade Cunningham at pick 5, Maxey, Jalen Johnson, Trae Young, Chet Holmgren, Jalen Brunson, Donovan Clingan, Walker Kessler, Stephon Castle, Alex Sarr and Miles Bridges. His recurring reason is less usage available because teammates are coming back or have been added. He also opens with injury news: Ariel Hukporti tore his Achilles, which weakens Philadelphia's backup center spot.

rules.text: A bust here does not mean a player you should never draft. It means his current draft spot is too high. The margin depends on the round: a few spots matters in round one, about 20 spots in round six.
rules.quote: Four, five spots might be too high in round one. 20 spots is probably too high

rules.text: Yahoo rankings are not tied to a league format. The same player can be very different in value in points leagues and category leagues, so adjust for your format.
rules.quote: Always remember Yahoo ranks are nondescript. They don't mean anything because they're not specific to a league format.

rules.text: Players returning from an Achilles tear can have an efficiency dip and lose minutes early in the season.
rules.quote: plus returning from an Achilles you can see a dip in efficiency look at Deonte look at Jason Tatum

rules.text: Players who rush back for opening night from calf or hamstring injuries risk a minutes restriction and getting hurt again.
rules.quote: if they push to get back for opening night and White did this last season, you'd be on a minutes restriction

rules.text: Look at usage trends across the season, not just full-season averages, especially when a player's usage was boosted by teammates being out.
rules.quote: This is where all the trends and all that sort of stuff are important to note.

rules.text: Price in a 'finals tax'. Players coming off a championship run may get extra rest or slightly regress.
rules.quote: We can just throw the the finals tax onto this as well if you want.

rules.text: Near the top of a draft, a pick's quality can come down to two or three spots. Later in the draft the gaps are much wider and small differences matter less.
rules.quote: the difference between like whether it's a good or a bad pick might only be two or three spots.

rules.text: When drafting Giannis, it still probably makes sense to punt free throws, even if your team ends up with decent free throw percentage.
rules.quote: That is not to say that you shouldn't punt free throws with Giannis. By the way, it still probably makes sense

rules.text: In head-to-head he does not value low turnovers. Blocks are heavily right-skewed, so z-score rankings overstate shot blockers.
rules.quote: I don't care about low turnovers. blocks are so heavily right skewed that their zed score equivalent on them gives you false ideas

rules.text: Standard 9-cat rankings fail to show a player's real value in head-to-head. He prefers his own head-to-head per game ranks.
rules.quote: if you want an illustration of how that that ranking system doesn't illustrate the value of a player

rules.text: An ADP that sits between points league and category league value is wrong for both formats.
rules.quote: this ADP is sort of just splitting the middle. It's not a points league ADP. It's not a category league ADP.

rules.text: Low-scoring bigs taken early hurt you, because after rounds three or four it is hard to find enough scoring to make up for them.
rules.quote: when you can't really get big scoring players after round three or four. You get his 12 points per game

rules.text: Usage is limited: one ball, one shot per possession. Projections for teammates have to balance against each other.
rules.quote: There's one ball. There's one shot attempt per possession. There's one guy who can dribble at a time.

rules.text: If a player like Miles Bridges is the number one option on a team, that team is bad.
rules.quote: If Miles Bridges is the number one option, your team sucks.
